headline: How Freshpet Earned AI’s Trust: A GEO & AI Visibility Playbook via @sejournal, @hethr_campbell
blog_article:
You’ve invested in content that customers love. They tell you your website is clear, your FAQs are thorough, and your product pages answer every question. But when you check your analytics, the numbers don’t reflect this enthusiasm. Even more puzzling, when you try searching for your business using voice assistants or AI-powered directories, you find incomplete details—or worse, your business is missing entirely. All that work, and somehow, you’re invisible at the moment discovery happens.

It’s a contradiction that’s becoming more common as AI systems take over the gatekeeping role in digital discovery. The assumption has always been: if your content is detailed, accurate, and helpful, it will naturally rise to the top in search results and recommendations. But AI doesn’t see your business the way your customers do. It doesn’t reward you for clarity or completeness alone.

Here’s the tension: AI platforms don’t just scan for content that’s useful to people—they scan for content that’s useful to machines. If your site isn’t structured in a way that algorithms can reliably parse, cite, and trust, your business can be erased from the digital map, no matter how much your customers value what you offer.

This isn’t just a theory. Businesses with comprehensive, customer-praised content are finding themselves left out of AI-powered discovery tools. The underlying mechanism is technical: AI systems prioritize structured, machine-readable data and authoritative citations. Content that lacks the right metadata or technical scaffolding is often deprioritized or omitted, regardless of its value to human readers.

Consider Freshpet, a company that manufactures and sells fresh, refrigerated pet food. Despite having a robust online presence, Freshpet found its information misrepresented or missing in AI-driven results. By partnering with Intero Digital, they restructured their content and refined their GEO strategies—not to change what they said, but to change how AI could see and cite them. The result: improved visibility, not because their content became more helpful to people, but because it became more legible to algorithms.

The consequence for any business is clear. When AI platforms decide what gets discovered, content that isn’t structured for algorithmic recognition can erase your business from digital channels. Your authority and reach shrink at the very moment someone is searching for what you offer.

The real barrier isn’t the helpfulness or detail of your content, but its inability to speak the technical language AI systems require to recognize and recommend it. Human-centric design alone is no longer enough when algorithms are the ones deciding what gets seen.

Where in your business is valuable content being overlooked because it isn’t structured for the systems that decide what gets seen?

A business can be present everywhere except in the places where AI is looking.

## Source

[Search Engine Journal](https://www.searchenginejournal.com/how-freshpet-earned-ais-trust-a-geo-ai-visibility-playbook-recap/588706/)
